head.i: Quæ habent in Ablativo singulari i tantum?

main_text.p: Neutra in al aut ar definentia: ut Vectigal, sol[?] ab hoc vectigali. Calcar, ein spor[?] ab hoc calcari. Præter, Sal, salʒ. Hepar, Die Läber. Far[?] Jubar, der schein vnd glantz eines feurigen dinges. Nectar, ein süß tranck der Heydnischen Götter: quæ e habent: ut, fale, hepate, farre, jubare, nectare.

Adjectiva unius terminationis e vel i habent: ut, amans, ab hoc amante vel amanti. Degener, degenere vel degeneri. Excipe, pauper, sopes[?] & alia nonnulla. Item & Comparativi e vel i habent: ut, Major, majore, vel majori.

head.i: Quæ habent in Nominativo plurali ia?

main_text.p: Neutra, quorum Ablativus singularis in i tantum, vel in e & i simul definit: ut, ab hoc vectigali, hæc vectigalia: ab hoc audace vel audaci, hæc audacia. Excipe, Vetus, vetera: Et Comparativos: ut Majora, plura Veteres plura & pluria dixere.

head.i: Quæ habent in Genitivo plurali ium?

main_text.p: Nomina, quorum Ablativus singularis in i tatum, vel in e & i simul exit: ut, ab hoc animali horum animalium. Ab hoc, hac, hoc fœlice, vel fœlici, horum, harum, horum fœlicium. Deinde ium habent, quorum Nominativus singularis in duas consonas exit: ut, pars, partium, ein theil. Falx, falciu, ein sichel/ oder Trum[?] schneidmesser. Merx, mercium, Kauffmans wahr/ oder gut. Sapiens, sapientium vel sapientum, weisse. Parens, parentium vel parentum, die eltern. Tertio monosyllaba quædam: ut, Cor, cordium. Lis, litium. Mas, marium. Mus, murium. Os, ossium.
Primo, Comparativi: ut, Major, majorum. Melior, meliorum. Plus habet plurium. Deinde hæc sequentia:

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the German glosses after "Vectigal" (sol[?]), "Calcar" (spor[?]), "Far[?]" and "Trum[?]" are hard to read at this scan quality. "sopes[?]" is read as one word. The heading "plurali ia?" and the page number "73[?]" are uncertain. The gloss "Tertio monosyllaba" line and the "ium" forms follow the printed order. The Latin "fale" is copied as printed.
